# `∞` — Infinity

Literal. Keys: `Alt-8`. Hanzi: `永`

`∞` and `¯∞` are approximate real infinities.

```bpl
∞+3                ⍝ ∞
3÷∞                ⍝ 0
⌊/⍬                ⍝ ∞
⌈/⍬                ⍝ ¯∞
```

`¯∞` < every finite real < `∞`. Each infinity equals itself. `⌊/` and `⌈/` of an empty array are infinite, even for exact arrays. Under dynamic kinds, the functions that [Infinities and NaN](../numbers.qmd#infinities-and-nan) lists raise `DOMAIN` where they have no result, as `∞∨2` does. Other undefined results with an infinity are NaN, as IEEE 754 defines:

```bpl
∞-∞                ⍝ $n
0×∞                ⍝ $n
```

[Infinities and NaN](../numbers.qmd#infinities-and-nan) covers how infinities combine with exact numbers.

## Errors

- `DOMAIN`: an infinite index or count
